Precondition: Terminal assigned to a Cell/machine; Downtime Manager reachable from the plant-floor header
Step: Open the Downtime Manager and start a new manual downtime event
Expected Result: A downtime event opens with the machine auto-populated from the terminal location; reason code, start time, and remarks are captured

Precondition: An open downtime event exists on this machine
Step: End the open event when the machine resumes
Expected Result: Event is closed (EndedAt set); duration is computed; the event is stamped with the operator

Precondition: Downtime Manager open
Step: Use Add-Past to record a fully-elapsed downtime event with start and end in the past
Expected Result: A closed historical event is recorded and shift-stamped; it appears in the terminal's event list

Precondition: PLC downtime is not yet commissioned for this line
Step: Confirm the PLC-stop watcher exists and a PLC-sourced event can carry a null reason for later assignment
Expected Result: Design supports source=PLC events with a null reason the operator assigns after the fact; PLC auto-trigger is commissioning-gated (watcher present, no-op until configured)

Precondition: A downtime event with source=PLC and no reason code
Step: Assign a reason code to the unclassified PLC-sourced event
Expected Result: Reason is bound after the fact and the event is reclassified

Precondition: A machine with an active (unended) downtime event
Step: View the machine's production screen / plant-floor header
Expected Result: The open event is shown prominently (line-down indicator); open events remain visible until closed

Precondition: An existing downtime event
Step: Attempt to edit the event's StartedAt
Expected Result: StartedAt is immutable and cannot be overwritten; only EndedAt, reason code, and remarks are editable

Precondition: An erroneous downtime event
Step: Void the event from the Downtime Manager
Expected Result: Event is soft-voided (append-only, no hard delete): marked voided with reason/user, closed if still open, excluded from rollups but still visible

Precondition: Downtime Manager open on a machine in a known area
Step: Select a reason type then pick a specific code
Expected Result: Reason codes are filtered by the machine's area and by reason type; operator selects the type first, then the code within it
Notes: Types: Equipment, Mold, Quality, Setup, Miscellaneous, Unscheduled

Precondition: A downtime event started within a shift window
Step: Inspect the event's shift association
Expected Result: Event is associated with the shift instance in which it started (ShiftId FK)

Precondition: A downtime event still open at a shift boundary
Step: Cross the shift boundary without resuming the machine
Expected Result: Event is not auto-split; it stays associated with the shift it started in and remains open until the incoming operator closes it

Precondition: Logged in on a dedicated-flavor terminal near scheduled shift end
Step: Open the shift end-time-entry control and toggle the breaks taken
Expected Result: A toggle button appears per scheduled break; tapping selects/deselects with no numeric duration entry; the control is visible only ~15 min before through ~15 min after scheduled shift end

Precondition: Break buttons toggled
Step: Submit the end-of-shift entry
Expected Result: One closed DowntimeEvent is written per selected break with duration resolved from the schedule (not operator-entered); one submission per operator per shift (re-submit rejected)

Workflow: End-of-shift time entry (shared flavor / zero breaks)
Precondition: Shared-flavor terminal at shift end
Step: Enter initials and submit with no breaks selected
Expected Result: Initials resolve to an AppUser and stamp the submission; selecting zero breaks is valid — no DowntimeEvent rows written but the shift-end acknowledgement is still recorded

Precondition: Production recorded before the scheduled shift start
Step: Record a production event with a timestamp earlier than scheduled start
Expected Result: Event is accepted without rejection; the availability window expands backward to the earliest event

Precondition: A scheduled shift with zero production events across its whole window
Step: Advance past the scheduled window and inspect the shift
Expected Result: An Oee.Shift instance is still created and reports as zero-run for auditability

Precondition: Terminal with open downtime, open LOT pauses, and in-process LOTs at its Cell
Step: Open the Shift-End Summary (or trigger Handover)
Expected Result: A read-only one-screen summary lists open downtime events, open LOT pauses, and in-process LOTs at the terminal's Cell(s)

Precondition: Shift-End Summary displayed
Step: Acknowledge the summary as the outgoing operator
Expected Result: Handover acknowledgement is recorded to Audit.OperationLog (ShiftHandoverAcknowledged); the summary is optional and may be skipped without affecting open events/pauses

Precondition: Die-cast production and rejects captured for a die over a shift
Step: Request a Die Shot report for a die and shift
Expected Result: Report shows total shots, good shots, warm-up shots, and reject counts per die per shift
Notes: Inputs captured (DieCastContribution/shift output); dedicated report screen pending in this build

Precondition: Rejects recorded with defect codes across machines
Step: Request a Rejects report filtered by defect code / area / machine / date range
Expected Result: Report shows reject counts grouped by defect code with area/machine/date-range filters
Notes: Inputs captured; dedicated report screen pending in this build

Precondition: Downtime events captured across a date range
Step: Request a Downtime report filtered by reason code / reason type / area / machine / date range
Expected Result: Report shows downtime events by reason code and type with total downtime minutes per shift
Notes: Inputs captured via Downtime Manager/DowntimeEvent; dedicated report/CSV-export screen pending in this build

Precondition: Production output recorded by part / machine / shift
Step: Request a Production summary report over a date range
Expected Result: Report summarizes output by part number, machine, and shift with good count, reject count, and yield
Notes: Inputs captured; dedicated report screen pending in this build

Precondition: A shift schedule active for the line
Step: Start and end a shift via events
Expected Result: Shift instances are event-derived at runtime (Shift_Start / Shift_End, toggle-per-break); no pre-computed minutes; the reconcile ticker snaps boundaries to schedule
